title: Outcome in Colorectal Cancer: Identification of Differences and Measures for Nationwide Quality Development
summary: Colorectal cancer is one of the most common cancers in Germany. The EDIUM study ("Outcome Quality in Colorectal Cancer: Identification of Differences and Measures for Nationwide Quality Development") compares the outcome quality after treatment nationwide. The results of the study serve to improve life with colorectal cancer in Germany. Besides clinical data, such as the size of the tumor or the type of treatment, patient-reported data on the health and treatment-related quality of life reported is collected. The patients are interviewed on the basis of an internationally recognized questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-30 and QLQ-C29) on their general well-being and physical fitness, on mental health problems and on physical problems. The survey takes place at two measuring times: before therapy and once again after 12 months. The total duration of the study is three years. Patients suffering from colorectal cancer for the first time and undergo surgery or palliative care can participate in more than 100 cancer cancer centers certified by the German Cancer Society.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- primary cases, that are introduced to the center for the first time
- patients with a colorectal carcinom
- patients that undergo elective surgery or non-surgical palliative therapy
Exclusion criteria:
- insufficient German language skills in order to answer the survey
